pagerduty-bot: :rotating_light: Pager P12345 fired — inference queue 'inference-prod' depth 15,432, queue growth rate 2k/min, autoscaler lagging (>10m). Runbook: https://redwood/runbooks/inference-queue
incident-bot: Alert group: capacity / autoscaler / queue-backlog. Target severity: SEV2.
alex: ack — I'm on it, switching to incident channel. ETA 5m to triage.
maria: seeing spike in 500s from hosted API (latency 1.8s -> 6s). Can we throttle non-critical traffic? :thinking_face:
alex: pulling autoscaler and cloud logs now. Pasting recent autoscaler lines:
```
2026-03-17T10:02:34Z autoscaler: desired_replicas=60 actual_nodes=18 pending_provision=0 failed_scale_attempts=8 reason=kubeapi_rate_limit
2026-03-17T10:02:50Z kubeapi: request_quota_exceeded client=scale-controller qps=0.5 burst=5
```
maria: kubeapi throttle — that explains stalled scale. If API is throttled manual kubectl won't help.
tyler: we can either divert traffic to the Dedicated pool or temporarily rate-limit free/PLG keys. Which is faster?
alex: divert is fastest. Executing traffic split (internal command): `routes set-weight inference-prod region-b 25%` — doing a 25% diversion to region-b-dedicated now.
pranav: infra will also trigger a nodepool scale via control plane (infra service) — I'm running: `infra scale-nodepool --pool inference-hot --count 60` per runbook step 2b. Sharing ticket INF-4781.
cs-rep: looping in CS — early customers may see errors, prepping note for affected customers.
incident-bot: Pager P12345 acked by alex. Escalation timer set to 10m for SEV1 if error rate stays elevated.
alex: enabling token throttles for free-tier clients and lowering concurrency header for some routes. Command: `config set-rate-limit --tag free-tier --rps 10`
maria: confirmation — started seeing fewer 500s after token throttles, but latency still high for large batches.
tyler: while infra scales, let's reduce batch sizes for inference to avoid spikes. Applying hotfix to router: `batch_size_override=8` (rolling).
alex: infra confirmed nodepool scale submitted, but cloud reports kubeapi errors are intermittent. Monitoring control-plane request metrics.
10m later — alex: nodepool reported 62 nodes ready, processing throughput up ~2.2x, queue depth down from 15,432 -> 4,120 in 8m. CPU on new nodes ~15%.
pranav: confirmed cloud throttling cleared after retries; we need a durable fix: increase controller-manager QPS/burst and add exponential backoff in our scale reconciler. Filing follow-up: INF-4792.
cs-rep: sent initial notification to top 10 affected accounts, offering mitigation guidance.
tyler: proposed post-incident tasks: (1) detect kubeapi throttle pattern earlier in autoscaler; (2) add fallback traffic diversion in controller; (3) update runbook with explicit infra command snippets.
alex: handing off to overnight oncall @sam with summary and todo: monitor queue until <500, verify no regression, follow INF-4792. Marking pager P12345 as under-control (not fully resolved). :thumbsup:
sam: taking handoff, ETA check at 02:00Z. Please add any outstanding checks I should run.
alex: checklist pasted to incident doc: 1) verify queue delta trend negative 2) confirm nodepool desired==ready 3) confirm no new kubeapi 429s in control-plane metrics 4) revert token throttles once stable. Link: https://redwood/incidents/P12345-haffoff
incident-bot: Noted. If queue doesn't drop below 500 in 90m, auto-escalate to SEV1.
pranav: adding long-term items to backlog: controller backoff, rate-limit auto-diversion, and improved alerting for autoscaler-silent-failures.
maria: thanks team — good coordination. Closing channel unless anything else crops up. :white_check_mark:
